verdict.rationale: Adyen documents a rule builder in its Protect risk system: merchants can create, backtest, and label custom rules, and every payment is evaluated to an automatic block, allow, or review action. That is real rule-to-action automation on payment events, but it is confined to fraud and risk decisions. Webhooks only notify your own server, which would have to implement the actions itself, so they earn no credit as a rules engine. missing for 10: general-purpose event-to-action rules beyond risk decisions (e.g. on refunds, disputes, payouts or onboarding events), detailed documentation of rule conditions and available actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.
